title: Pullback formula and rigidity of already-given compatible lifts
statement: Use [def-trf-large-oriented-site-data] and the same finite-limit sites, F,G,f,g,etaF,etaG. Suppose p1,p2 and comparisons pi1,pi2 are given and tau satisfies LargeOrientationFormula. Every already-given compatible lift (h,alpha,beta) of every cone (a,b,t) has the exact structural pullback square in LargeHasLiftFormula. For any two compatible lifts (h,alpha,beta) and (h2,alpha2,beta2), there exists a unique gamma:h.direct≅h2.direct such that whiskering gamma with p1.direct followed by alpha2 is alpha, and similarly for p2 and beta. No existence of a lift, no projection construction and no site-independence theorem is asserted.

source.place: ILO XI Lemma 1.5 and §1.6, uniqueness in Theorem 1.4; Lean: lean/Sheaf/CategoryTheory/Sites/OrientedProductLargeLiftRigidity.lean

proof.text: Prove the cartesian formula of XI Lemma 1.5 directly. For $Z=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ put $A=k_1(U)$, $B=k_2(W)$, $C_Z=(U\to V\leftarrow g^{-1}V)$ and $D_Z=(f^{-1}V\to V\leftarrow W)$. Componentwise pullbacks give $D_Z=T_V\times_{G_V}B$ and $Z=C_Z\times_{T_V}D_Z$. The arrow $C_Z\to A$ is type (c). Representable presheaves preserve these pullbacks by the universal property of a limit, and sheafification preserves them by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]. Cancelling the type-(c) isomorphisms $C_Z^a\cong A^a$ and $T_V^a\cong F_V^a$ therefore yields $Z^a\cong A^a\times_{G_V^a}B^a$. The map $A^a\to G_V^a$ here is $A^a\to F_V^a\xrightarrow{(r_V^a)^{-1}}T_V^a\to G_V^a$, since $C_Z\to T_V\to F_V$ equals $C_Z\to A\to F_V$. By step 4 this is the map induced by $U\to f^{-1}V$ followed by the inverse-image mate of $\tau$. Thus the bottom object is $(gp_2)^{-1}(V^a)$; no direct-image functor is applied to $V$. All these identifications are natural in morphisms of triples because their projections are the structural arrows just specified.

source.place: Exposé XI Lemma 1.5 and its cartesian-diagram proof

proof.text: Apply the inverse image of any compatible lift to the preceding pullback square. It preserves finite limits; projection comparisons identify its top arrows, and compatibility of pasted direct-image transformations identifies, after taking mates, the bottom arrows with those induced by t. This is exactly LargeHasLiftFormula, including the specified structural maps.

For two compatible lifts the resulting squares have the same bottom and side objects and maps. The unique isomorphism of their pullbacks is natural in Z and respects both projections. By adjunction and Yoneda the values of either direct image at a triple Z and object M are Hom from that pullback to M. These isomorphisms therefore define an isomorphism of sheaves, natural in M, hence of direct-image functors. Any projection-compatible isomorphism induces the same map on these pullbacks; evaluating its sheaf components on every triple forces equality. This gives existence and uniqueness of the asserted gamma. No existence of a compatible lift is used or claimed. Apply largeDirectImageIsoFromRepresentables from [lem-trf-large-oriented-representable-comparison] to the natural isomorphisms on inverse-image restrictions. Its construction extends the isomorphism and its inverse and its uniqueness forces equality of any other projection-compatible comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem largeCompatibleLiftRigidity
    (hτ : LargeOrientationFormula F G J₁ J₂ K f g ηF ηG p₁ p₂ π₁ π₂ τ) :
    LargeHasLiftFormula.{v, w, e, ve} F G J₁ J₂ K f g ηF ηG p₁ p₂ π₁ π₂ τ ∧
    ∀ (E : Type e) [Category.{ve} E], IsGrothendieckTopos.{max v w} E →
      ∀ (a : GeometricMorphism E (Sheaf J₁.toGrothendieck (Type (max v w))))
        (b : GeometricMorphism E (Sheaf J₂.toGrothendieck (Type (max v w))))
        (t : (b.comp g).direct ⟶ (a.comp f).direct)
        (h h' : GeometricMorphism E (Sheaf (largeTopology J₁ J₂ F G) (Type (max v w))))
        (α : (h.comp p₁).direct ≅ a.direct) (β : (h.comp p₂).direct ≅ b.direct)
        (α' : (h'.comp p₁).direct ≅ a.direct) (β' : (h'.comp p₂).direct ≅ b.direct),
        paste f g p₁ p₂ τ h a b α β = t →
        paste f g p₁ p₂ τ h' a b α' β' = t →
        ∃! γ : h.direct ≅ h'.direct,
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight γ p₁.direct ≪≫ α' = α ∧
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight γ p₂.direct ≪≫ β' = β
